summary: Refactored DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests to use shared MySqlConnection + MySqlTransaction rolled back in Dispose (AC-1). Added NonDisposingConnection wrapper (suppresses Close/Dispose so SUT's 'using var' does not close the shared session) and SharedConnectionFactory that returns wrapped connections. CreateCommand() overridden to auto-enlist every Dapper command in the shared transaction — required by MySqlConnector when a connection-level transaction is active. QueryDirect<T> helper added for assertion reads on the shared connection (passes transaction parameter explicitly). DELETE-based Dispose cleanup removed. SpdbConfigLibraryFolderRepositoryTests already satisfies all applicable ACs with its existing DELETE-cleanup pattern (rollback-based isolation cannot be applied because that repository commits atomically within its own methods, as documented in its test class comment). All other ACs (no DDL, no Commit(), vi_test_ prefixes, skip-without-config) were already met by the existing test files.
Final test suite: 92 VideoIndexer.Tests + 92 VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests (4 skipped) + 48 VideoIndexer.App.Tests = 232 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail.

comments.note: DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests: the NonDisposingConnection.CreateCommand() override relies on MySqlConnector's requirement that commands must specify the active transaction. This is a MySqlConnector-specific behaviour (unlike SQL Server which auto-enlists). If the driver is ever swapped, the override can be removed. Worth a brief comment in the test class.

DapperMovieCatalogRepository creates a new connection per method call (no ambient transaction support). This pattern prevents transactional composition at the caller level and makes rollback-based test isolation non-trivial. If multi-operation transactions are ever needed in production, the connection factory pattern will need to be extended with an IUnitOfWork or IDbTransaction-passing overload.

summary: Full QA pass on WP-014. Build verified (0 warnings, 0 errors). All 6 acceptance criteria confirmed.

AC-1 (rollback isolation): Verified — _sharedTransaction.Rollback() in Dispose(); all SUT operations route through NonDisposingConnection.CreateCommand() which pre-enrolls each MySqlCommand in the shared transaction.
AC-2 (no DDL): Grep confirmed — zero CREATE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE statements across both test files.
AC-3 (no Commit): Grep confirmed — zero .Commit() calls in test files. Only Rollback() in Dispose.

AC-5 (self-skip): Each test calls Skip.If(_skipReason is not null, _skipReason) with actionable skip message identifying the missing config file and env var.
AC-6 (live DB): 9/9 tests passed against live MariaDB instance. Full regression: 232 passed, 4 pre-existing skipped, 0 failed.

comments.note: Rollback isolation mechanism verified: SharedConnectionFactory returns NonDisposingConnection wrapping the shared MySqlConnection. NonDisposingConnection.CreateCommand() pre-enrolls every MySqlCommand in the shared transaction. Dispose() always calls _sharedTransaction.Rollback(). Since DapperMovieCatalogRepository.InsertMovieAsync uses connection.ExecuteAsync (which calls CreateCommand()), all inserts participate in the shared transaction and are correctly rolled back.
No DDL (CREATE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE) or Commit() calls found anywhere in the test files (grep confirmed). AC-2 and AC-3 fully satisfied.
All test hashes use 'VI_TEST_MCR_' prefix and filenames use '/vi_test_mcr/' path prefix — clearly distinct from production data. AC-4 satisfied.

Tests ran against a live MariaDB instance and all 9/9 passed. No Skipped results, confirming the test-config.json is present in this environment. Skip logic verified by code inspection (Skip.If(_skipReason is not null, _skipReason) in each test).

summary: Code review PASS. WP-014 reviewed: DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests.cs (modified).

The NonDisposingConnection + SharedConnectionFactory rollback isolation pattern is architecturally correct and well-suited to MySqlConnector's requirement that commands explicitly enlist in the active transaction. Dispose() always calls Rollback(), ensuring no test data escapes to the database.

All 9 test methods follow consistent skip/test/assert structure. The QueryDirect<T> helper correctly passes the shared transaction to assertion queries so they see uncommitted inserts. All vi_test_ prefixes are consistent throughout.
The #pragma warning disable CS8767 for the ConnectionString setter is appropriate and correctly scoped.

comments.note: DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests.cs: The NonDisposingConnection + SharedConnectionFactory rollback isolation pattern is correct and well-documented. The CreateCommand() override is necessary for MySqlConnector (which requires explicit transaction enrollment on commands) and the XML doc explains this constraint clearly. Dispose() always calls Rollback() ensuring no writes survive.

DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests.cs: QueryDirect<T> uses _sharedConnection! (null-forgiving). This is safe by invariant: every test method calls Skip.If(_skipReason is not null, _skipReason) before calling CreateSut() or QueryDirect(), so _sharedConnection is guaranteed non-null when QueryDirect is reached. Not a concern.

DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests.cs: The CS8767 pragma suppressing nullable mismatch on ConnectionString setter is appropriate. IDbConnection.ConnectionString has [AllowNull] on the setter (pre-NRT design), but MySqlConnection.ConnectionString setter is non-nullable. Using a targeted pragma restore pair is the correct approach here.

DapperMovieCatalogRepositoryTests.cs: InsertMovieAsync_InsertsRowWithEmptyMetadataDefaults verifies all 12 columns including their exact empty/zero/null defaults. This is a valuable regression safety net for the INSERT statement schema. The MovieRow sealed record DTO pattern is clean.
